A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MF-LLM and IB-Tune study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original WEIBO simulations, quantitative baseline comparisons, component ablations, intervention experiments, and generated-comment analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and reports revised training-loss and detailed simulation curves in its appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same mean-field/policy interaction, warm-up procedure, IB-based mean-field optimization, policy likelihood objective, and historical-state sampling. V3 reformats the pseudocode and expresses the mean-field objective as a temporal sum without establishing a different algorithm or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both use the WEIBO corpus across the same seven domains and retain the rumor, retirement, speech-freedom, forecasting, intervention, and exogenous-signal scenarios. The revised illustration in Figure 1 does not introduce additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: State, Recent, Popular, and SFT retain their corresponding comparison roles. The cross-backbone comparisons and six component-ablation variants also retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the semantic-evaluation description from multiple events with up to 300 timesteps to 20 events with up to 300 agents. Both appendices still specify 14 scenarios and agent indices 50–300, leaving the actual sample count unclear. This establishes a reported-setting revision, not a confirmed rerun; splits, metrics, and training hyperparameters otherwise match.

E4.justification: The existing convergence and detailed rumor-dynamics analyses receive revised plotted evidence in v3 Figures 7–8, corresponding to v1 Figures 8–7. Their analytical questions and variant sets remain unchanged, as do the intervention, exogenous-signal, and generated-comment case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both describe the training-curve shading as unsmoothed loss fluctuations and use the same moving-average window, rather than statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The mean-field training-loss curve changes from ending near −5 in v1 Figure 8 to approximately −17 in v3 Figure 7. Several sentiment, attitude, and stance trajectories and associated divergence curves also change in the detailed appendix simulation figure. Main Tables 1–2, the dimensional-results table renumbered from 3 to 4, and Figures 2–6 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix D.1 adds a derivation of the variational KL upper bound on the information-bottleneck compression term, which v1 Section 3.2 only states. This supplies mathematical justification for an existing objective rather than introducing a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: V3 explicitly claims to be the first framework incorporating mean-field theory into LLM-based social simulation, adding a priority claim absent from v1. The central feedback-modeling, IB-Tune, 47% KL reduction, generalization, and application claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explicit limitations paragraph acknowledging the lack of real-time external-signal detection/integration and compounding errors over long simulation horizons. It proposes recalibration and error-aware feedback, qualifying the retained fidelity claims beyond v1's discussion of future signal injection.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix A newly specifies two NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB GPUs, CUDA and driver versions, and training times of approximately 74, 64, and 25 hours for the mean-field, policy, and SFT models. Existing hyperparameters and prompts are retained; the relocated repository link identifies the same resource.

R1.justification: V3 adds Monti et al.'s On learning agent-based models from data and removes CAMEL, Cooperate or Collapse, and LLM Voting. It also emphasizes mean-field approximation and adds an explicit first-integration claim. Much of the existing related-work discussion moves to Appendix E.

P1.justification: The abstract, motivation, contributions, method exposition, experiment narrative, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. V3 separates the problem statement, condenses main-text related work, moves detailed setup into the appendix, reorders appendix sections, and adds an appendix contents list.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the retirement illustration with a rumor example and adds a trend-comparison inset. Existing figures and tables are regrouped and resized, training-plot axes change, and captions receive edits. Most chart designs and table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: V3 improves the existing study's accessibility and reproducibility through clearer organization, hardware/runtime disclosure, an explicit IB-bound derivation, and more candid limitations. These gains are tempered by the new 20-event description conflicting with the retained 14-scenario appendix and a derivation sentence calling a nonpositive term non-negative. The main empirical evidence remains largely unchanged.
